segments.title: Graf Spee races back into the Atlantic
segments.body: Admiral Graf Spee is back in the Atlantic after Hans Langsdorff hurried through its previous operating areas. The ship is heading for a rendezvous with Altmark and preparing for the next stage of its cruise. It would still attack a suitable target if one appeared. For now, preparations to keep the raider ready and protected take precedence over hunting merchant shipping.

evidence.note: The transcript describes Graf Spee's rapid Atlantic return, its approach to an Altmark rendezvous, and preparations taking priority over hunting targets.

segments.summary: Graf Spee returns quickly to the Atlantic, where preparations for the next phase take precedence over immediate commerce raiding.

segments.title: Altmark provides supplies for Graf Spee's disguises
segments.body: The 24 November meeting with the supply ship Altmark gives Admiral Graf Spee fuel and materials for making disguises. Altmark has been carrying supplies throughout the cruise. Stores taken from captured merchant ships provide another source of materials. The preparations at this rendezvous support the continued journeys of both Graf Spee and Altmark.

evidence.note: The transcript dates the Altmark rendezvous to 24 November, identifies Altmark and merchant ships as sources of stores, and connects the supplies to disguise construction and preparations for both vessels' continued journeys.
The recap explicitly describes Graf Spee as refuelling and building disguises.

segments.summary: At the 24 November rendezvous, Altmark provides fuel and supplies used to fabricate disguises and prepare Graf Spee for the rest of its raiding cruise.

segments.title: Altmark takes prisoners and perhaps more weapons
segments.body: Altmark receives more prisoners from Graf Spee, including captured merchant seamen and some officers. The supply ship already has a couple of machine guns from the raider, and further weapons may have followed at this meeting. The date of that additional transfer is uncertain: some chronologies place it earlier or later than 24 November. This rendezvous seems the likeliest opportunity because the ships faced less immediate pressure and were receiving substantial replenishments, so the prisoner movement is more securely dated than the possible weapons transfer.

evidence.note: The transcript describes prisoner transfers, says Altmark already had a couple of machine guns from Graf Spee, and explains why 24 November is suggested as the uncertain date of a further weapons transfer.

segments.summary: Graf Spee transfers more captured merchant seamen and officers to Altmark, which already carries machine guns supplied by the raider. Further guns may have passed between the ships during the same quiet rendezvous, but their timing is uncertain.

segments.title: Forces H and K search behind Graf Spee
segments.body: Between 20 November and 2 December, the Royal Navy's Forces H and K pass through Graf Spee's former Atlantic cruising grounds and move far south, almost to the Indian Ocean. Earlier in the cruise, the raider had moved more slowly than the British expected. The hunters therefore timed their arrival on the assumption that Langsdorff was still taking his time, with enough fuel and supplies to watch the area for about six days. Graf Spee had since accelerated its movements, and Langsdorff had already passed through before they could intercept it.

evidence.note: The transcript maps Forces H and K southward, describes their six-day patrol endurance, and explains that Graf Spee's earlier slow progress shaped British expectations before Langsdorff accelerated and passed the interception area.

segments.summary: Graf Spee's earlier slow progress leads the British to expect another slow passage, but Langsdorff's rapid return to the Atlantic puts the raider past Forces H and K before they can intercept it.

segments.title: Forces H and K are absent from the River Plate battle
segments.body: After 2 December, the hunter groups turn north. The move leaves them far from South America when Graf Spee meets the British cruisers at the Battle of the River Plate on 13 December. Their failed southern search explains why Forces H and K were not close enough to join the later battle. Ships assigned to hunt the raider could not influence the engagement because they had been sent toward its earlier cruising area.

evidence.note: The transcript says the groups returned north and were consequently distant when the Battle of the River Plate occurred on 13 December.

segments.summary: When the southern search ends, the hunter groups turn north and remain far from the 13 December Battle of the River Plate.
